analysis.title: Which way forward?
key_insights: Equities fell on disappointing earnings, led by tech: Korea's Kospi -3.5% and Nasdaq 100 -2%.

Attention is shifting to the US midterm elections next week and the risk of renewed US-Iran escalation after the polls close. Oil rose to its highest level since April on evidence of possible new US strikes on Iran.

Diplomacy attempts this week made no progress. Statements from President Trump and US and Israeli logistical preparations suggest military strikes may restart after November 3. The WSJ reports Trump was recently briefed on attack options.

Rabobank's global and energy strategists assume the US, Israel and a broader Arab and European coalition are likely to attack Iran and the Houthis and defend Saudi Arabia. Iran and the Houthis would probably hit Gulf countries and potentially Egypt, with fighting lasting until the end of 2027Q1 at varying intensity.

Main energy concern is diesel and marine fuel oils. Nearly 12% of world refining capacity is offline due to the Iran and Ukraine wars. The only path to lower prices and rising inventories is double de-escalation in both Russia-Ukraine and US-Iran. Rabobank is revising its refined products forecasts higher.

ECB left policy unchanged. Lagarde said inflation will stay well above target in coming quarters and that the ECB debated a hike. She hinted at a December hike, though messaging was not strictly hawkish.

The Governing Council does not see greater second-round effect risk than in September, even with energy prices above the ECB baseline. Rabobank reads this as the ECB expecting a stronger negative growth impact, limiting wage and price passthrough.

Leaked ECB estimates say the recent rise in bond yields subtracts about 1 percentage point from 2027-2028 growth and 90 basis points from inflation versus the September baseline. Rabobank reads this as the ECB hoping to pause after a December hike.

Lagarde leaves the ECB after the February meeting. Schnabel moves to the IMF at the start of 2027 and Lane's term ends in May. Rabobank sees Knot and De Cos as frontrunners for the presidency. French bond market turmoil and French elections add risk for the successor.

Eurozone Q3 GDP is due today, with Bloomberg consensus at +0.2% q/q. Ireland's 5.5% growth adds about 17bp to the aggregate. French Q3 GDP contracted 0.1% q/q, with household consumption +0.4% q/q boosted by hot-weather electricity demand and investment and exports a drag. IT equipment investment was the exception.
Other data today: Italy and Germany October inflation estimates and Canada August GDP.
earnings_insights: Disappointing earnings reports weighed on equity markets, led by tech shares. No company-level figures are given.

risk_factors: Renewed US-Iran escalation after the US midterms, with Iran and the Houthis attacking Gulf states and possibly Egypt.
Double escalation in Russia-Ukraine and the Middle East would deepen inventory declines in diesel and fuels.
Persistent energy inflation and tighter financial conditions from higher bond yields.
French fiscal and political risk and possible contagion around the ECB succession.
Deteriorating consumer sentiment in the Eurozone.

tension_points.bull_case: Diplomatic attempts continue, and double de-escalation in Iran and Ukraine is the only path to lower prices and rising inventories.
tension_points.bear_case: Trump statements, US and Israeli logistical preparations and a WSJ report of attack-option briefings suggest strikes may restart after November 3, with fighting lasting until end of 2027Q1.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Double de-escalation in both Russia-Ukraine and US-Iran wars would lower oil and fuel prices.
